programs.text_full:
🌿 Beyond Psychedelics, Yet Not Without

A Dialogue on Psychedelics, Contemplative Practice & Living Wisdom

with Roman Hanis & Kelly Yi, PhD
October 2, 2026 | 7:30–10:00 PM
San Francisco Bay Area, California

Psychedelics can catalyze experiences that radically change our perception of ourselves and reality. But what allows those experiences to mature into lasting transformation?

And what happens when we place psychedelics back into a much larger conversation about human development, contemplative practice, psychology, initiation, community, and the living wisdom traditions that have explored consciousness for centuries?

Beyond Psychedelics, Yet Not Without is an evening dialogue between Roman Hanis, co-founder of Paititi Institute and author of Beyond Ayahuasca, and Kelly Yi, PhD, psychologist, educator, author, and longtime contemplative practitioner.

Rather than approaching psychedelics as either the answer or something we need to leave behind, Roman and Kelly will explore their place within a more complete path of transformation. Psychedelic experiences can reveal dimensions of consciousness that profoundly challenge our habitual identity, yet insight alone does not necessarily resolve trauma, conditioning, attachment, projection, or the patterns through which we relate to ourselves and others.

This is not a new dilemma. Indigenous and contemplative traditions have developed sophisticated ways of approaching transformation within much larger cultural and developmental contexts. Medicine, meditation, ritual, breath, relationship with nature, psychological inquiry, community, disciplined practice, and initiation can all serve different functions along the way.

Drawing from Amazonian and Andean living wisdom traditions, Tibetan contemplative practice, Jungian and transpersonal psychology, somatic awareness, psychedelic experience and integration, Roman and Kelly will explore questions such as:

  • What can psychedelics reveal, and what can they not accomplish for us?
  • What is the relationship between a profound experience and the slow transformation of psychological conditioning?
  • How do awakening and psychological development relate to one another?
  • What role did initiation once play in guiding human development, and what might it mean today?
  • How can ancient and Indigenous systems of knowledge enter into dialogue with modern psychology without being stripped of their cultural context?
  • What does a sustained path of transformation look like when the emphasis shifts from accumulating extraordinary experiences toward how we actually live?

🌿 An Experiential Interlude

Halfway through the evening, Roman will guide participants through a brief standing Amazonian-based tribal breathwork practice, using synchronized breath, rhythm, sound, movement, and awareness.

Rather than only speaking about altered perception and embodied transformation, this short practice will offer a direct experiential point of reference for the second half of the conversation. It draws from the Amazonian breath tradition Roman has carried and practiced for more than two decades and forms part of the broader Primordial Breathwork approach taught through Paititi Institute.

The evening will conclude with open dialogue and Q&A, giving participants an opportunity to bring their own experience and questions into the conversation.

About Kelly Yi, PhD

Kelly Yi, PhD is a psychologist, educator, author, and Lead Faculty at Sofia University’s Master of Arts in Transpersonal Psychology Korea program. He is the author of Multidimensional Psychology and creator of the Multi-Dimensional Holistic Transformation framework, which integrates body, emotion, mind, attention, and nondual awareness.

His work brings together clinical practice, contemplative inquiry, somatic awareness, and community-based pathways for healing and transformation.

About Roman Hanis

Roman Hanis is the co-founder of Paititi Institute and author of the international bestselling book Beyond Ayahuasca: Unlocking the Evolutionary Science of Indigenous Amazonian Wisdom to Access Your Highest Potential.

For more than two decades, Roman’s path has developed through direct apprenticeship and relationship with Indigenous elders of the Amazon and Andes alongside sustained engagement with Tibetan contemplative traditions, Jungian psychology, Traditional Chinese Medicine, Qigong, and experiential approaches to healing and human transformation.

Through Paititi Institute, this work extends beyond retreats and individual healing into Indigenous cultural preservation, ancestral education, ecological stewardship, and the development of living bridges between ancestral knowledge and contemporary life.

Event Details

Date: Friday, October 2, 2026
Time: 7:30–10:00 PM
Location: San Francisco Bay Area, California
Exact venue details forthcoming.

No previous experience with psychedelics, breathwork, meditation, or any particular spiritual tradition is necessary.

Beyond Psychedelics, Yet Not Without is an invitation to examine psychedelics within the much wider territory of human transformation: honoring what these experiences can reveal while asking what it actually takes to embody those realizations in the way we live.

Roman Hanis

Roman Hanis is an international bestselling author, healer, educator, and co-founder of Paititi Institute, a nonprofit organization dedicated to Indigenous cultural preservation, healing, education, and ecological stewardship.

Since arriving in the Peruvian Amazon in 2001, Roman has spent decades studying, practicing, and collaborating with Indigenous knowledge holders of the Amazon and Andes. His path has included long-term apprenticeship and relationship with Yahua, Huitoto, Ashuar, Shipibo and other Amazonian traditions, alongside ongoing study and practice within Andean lineages. In 2004, following several years of apprenticeship in the Amazon, he was formally recognized as a curandero by Yahua elders, a responsibility he continues to honor through healing work, cultural exchange, education, and community initiatives.

Roman is the author of Beyond Ayahuasca: Unlocking the Evolutionary Science of Indigenous Amazonian Wisdom to Access Your Highest Potential, published by Hay House. Drawing upon more than two decades of lived experience in the Amazon, the book brings ancestral approaches to healing into dialogue with Jungian psychology, trauma resolution, Eastern medicine, and contemplative practice. 100% of Roman’s author proceeds from the book support the development of the Yahua Ancestral School and Cultural Heritage Center in the Peruvian Amazon.

As co-founder of Paititi Institute, Roman has helped develop intercultural healing retreats, Indigenous community health and cultural exchange initiatives, educational programs, and ecological conservation projects in Peru and internationally. The Institute also stewards a 1,516-hectare biocultural reserve spanning Andean foothills and cloud rainforest near Manu National Park, protecting a landscape where biological and cultural diversity remain deeply interconnected.

Alongside his Amazonian and Andean apprenticeships, Roman has spent decades studying and practicing Jungian psychology, Tibetan Buddhist and Bön traditions, Daoist internal arts, and Traditional Chinese Medicine. His work explores the resonances between these distinct traditions without reducing their differences, bringing their practical methods into an experiential approach to healing, self-knowledge, and the realization of our intrinsic relationship with the living world.

Roman’s own recovery from a severe, life-threatening period of Crohn’s disease in 2002 became an important turning point in this path. Today, his work is centered on creating experiential bridges through which ancestral knowledge can remain a living transmission while supporting both individual transformation and the communities and ecosystems from which these traditions arise.

programs.text_full:
Amazon New Year Retreat

16-Day Embodying True Nature Immersion

December 21, 2026 to January 5, 2027
Peruvian Amazon Rainforest, Iquitos, Peru

Begin the New Year in the Heart of the Amazon

Enter the New Year immersed in the Peruvian Amazon rainforest through a 16-day journey of remembrance, initiation, healing and self-discovery into the infinite potential of what it means to be a human being and embodiment of your true nature.

Embodying True Nature is Paititi Institute’s most comprehensive retreat process, supported by Amazonian, Andean and Tibetan living wisdom traditions with a set of foundational practices that have developed through more than two decades of experiential integration. These include Remembrance, Indigenous based Primordial Breathwork™, Indigenous and Jungian transpersonal based Dreamwork, Symptomatic Dance and Sacred Geometry, supported by Daoist and Andean Qigong, meditation, medicinal plants, sacred plant ceremonies, movement, creative expression, self-inquiry and integration.

The sacred plant traditions we work with include Ayahuasca from the Amazon, San Pedro or Huachuma and the sacred relationship with Coca from the Andes, each approached within its respective cultural and cosmological context. Sacred plant ceremonies are integral to the retreat, yet within the Indigenous traditions from which they emerge they belong to a much greater process involving relationship with nature, cosmovision, initiation, ancestral practices, community and the practical integration into everyday life.

Through this immersion we learn to recognize more clearly the individual and collective conditioning through which we perceive ourselves and our circumstances, while developing an experiential relationship with the essential nature that remains present beneath accumulated patterns of conditioning. The retreat is ultimately concerned with how this recognition can become embodied, so that transformation is not limited to an extraordinary experience in the rainforest but continues through the relationships, challenges and responsibilities of one’s daily life.

Program Details

Dates: December 21, 2026 to January 5, 2027
Duration: 16 days / 15 nights
Location: Amazon rainforest, approximately one hour outside Iquitos, Peru, accessible by boat
Contribution: $2,333 to $2,777 USD sliding scale
Accommodation: Traditional rainforest accommodations in shared rooms, with private rooms offered when available
Meals: Natural nourishing food appropriate to the retreat and medicinal plant work
Participation: Application and health screening required
Preparation: Accepted participants receive preparation guidance and lifelong access to Paititi’s self-paced online course, Your Evolutionary Blueprint

An Invitation

This retreat is about remembering and embodying who we truly are by stepping outside many of the habitual structures of everyday life and entering into sustained relationship with ourselves, the living intelligence of the Amazon and ancestral practices that have been carried through generations as ways of directly realizing the nature of human existence.

Over sixteen days, the different dimensions of the process continually inform one another as we learn to recognize the conditioning, emotional tensions, habitual patterns and unresolved experiences through which our energy and perception have become limited. The intention is to transform these patterns through self-realization, letting go, and reintegrating within a wider recognition of our innate nature and shared evolutionary potential of humanity’s shared heart.

Applications are now open.

MORE INFO:

View the Information & Preparation Document >>

So Much More Than a Plant Medicine Retreat

Sacred plant ceremonies are integral to the Indigenous ancestral traditions that inform this retreat, yet they have never existed in isolation from the greater cultural context that gives them meaning. This context includes cosmovision, creation stories and mythology, relationship with the natural world, dreams, prayer, diet, movement, breath, community, initiation, discipline and the responsibilities through which an individual finds their place within the greater eco-system.

In recent decades, sacred entheogenic plants have attracted people from nearly every part of contemporary society, often because they can temporarily open dimensions of experience beyond the habitual structures of logical and conceptual thinking. Within the living traditions from which these practices emerge, however, ceremonial experience has always belonged to a much broader process, and what may be revealed within a ceremony requires preparation, maturity, practice and integration if it is to become meaningful within one’s everyday life.

For this reason, Paititi approaches sacred plant work through an integral process of preparation, initiation, embodied practice and integration. Ceremonial experiences are supported by foundational practices that help participants recognize subconscious patterns, release emotional tensions, become increasingly receptive to the languages of the organism and nature, and develop practical ways of continuing the process after leaving the rainforest.

Remembering Our True Nature

Beyond the diverse stories, personalities and circumstances through which we have learned to know ourselves, there is a profound mystery within each human being and an innate potential that the organism continually seeks to remember.

Living wisdom traditions throughout the world have preserved rites of passage and experiential practices through which human beings can consciously participate in this process. Long before written history, these traditions recognized that human development does not end with biological maturity or the construction of a functional social identity, but can continue through an inner evolutionary journey in which accumulated conditioning gradually becomes transparent and deeper dimensions of consciousness become directly recognizable.

At the heart of this retreat is the recognition that beneath our defenses, habitual identities, personal histories and unconscious patterns lies an innate state of awareness, loving kindness, interconnectedness and presence that we refer to as True Nature.

At the same time, our lives continually communicate an evolutionary blueprint through relationships, dreams, symptoms, challenges, attractions, fears and circumstances. Much of this communication remains unconscious because we perceive experience through layers of personal and collective conditioning, and the emotions or experiences that have not been fully metabolized can remain embedded within the organism, where they continue influencing our perception and behavior while binding considerable amounts of vitality.

Through remembrance, initiation and direct experiential practice, these patterns can gradually become visible and the energy held within them can become available again. Experiences that previously seemed unrelated may then begin to reveal their relationship within a larger developmental process, allowing the difficulties and circumstances of one’s actual life to be understood as part of the evolutionary journey rather than as something separate from the path of self-realization.

The Foundational Practices

The Embodying True Nature process has developed through more than two decades of direct relationship with millennial living wisdom traditions of the Amazon, Andes and Tibet, with support from complementary Daoist, Jungian and transpersonal approaches. Certain practices serve as foundations throughout the retreat because they provide experiential ways of recognizing the different languages through which consciousness, the subconscious, emotions, nature and the organism continually communicate.

Remembrance

Remembrance is a foundational practice of releasing personal history through an energetic process of remembering, recognizing and letting go of subconscious limitations and emotional tensions held within one’s past.

Rather than depending primarily on intellectual analysis, the practice allows memories, emotions and embodied patterns to emerge within awareness so that what has remained unresolved can be experienced from a different level of consciousness. As identification with personal history begins to loosen, the energy invested in maintaining those patterns can gradually become available for a more direct and wholehearted experience of the present.

Primordial Breathwork™

Primordial Breathwork™ is a tribal practice integrating breath, rhythm, sound and awareness, inspired by Amazonian Indigenous breath traditions together with a Tibetan pre-Buddhist shamanic Bonpo tradition connected with the Heart Drops of Dharmakaya Dzogchen teachings.

Through synchronized breathing accompanied by live rhythm and sound, dimensions of cellular and emotional memory that may remain inaccessible through conceptual understanding can become experientially available. The process can catalyze cathartic release and recognition of deeply seated emotional obscurations while providing an embodied bridge between ceremonial experiences, subconscious material and ordinary consciousness.

Indigenous and Jungian Transpersonal based Dreamwork

Dreams have always held an important place within Amazonian cultures, where the distinction between dream and waking experience is often understood very differently from the dominant Western psychological perspective.

Our approach works particularly with perspectives received through the Ashuar tradition, together with Jungian and transpersonal approaches to the symbolic and associative language of the unconscious. Through individual and collective dreamwork, participants learn to recognize how dreams communicate aspects of their process that may not yet be available to the conscious personality, including recurring symbolic and archetypal patterns related to the evolutionary movement of one’s life.

Symptomatic Dance

The organism continually communicates through sensation, tension, movement, emotion and symptoms, yet we are commonly conditioned to suppress uncomfortable manifestations before developing a relationship with what they may be communicating.

Symptomatic Dance approaches this language experientially through movement and awareness, allowing participants to enter into relationship with embodied patterns and explore the unresolved energy that may be held within them. In this way, the body itself becomes an active participant in self-inquiry rather than merely something carried through a psychological or spiritual process.

Sacred Geometry

Sacred Geometry deepens our archetypal relationship with nature and with the universal patterns through which energy organizes itself. Rather than remaining an intellectual study of symbolic forms, it becomes an experiential practice through which patterns observed throughout the natural world can illuminate corresponding movements within our own organism and consciousness.

Together, these foundational practices provide a common language that accompanies participants throughout the retreat, allowing ceremonial experiences, dreams, symptoms, emotions and encounters with nature to be understood within one integrated process.

Sacred Plant Traditions

The retreat engages three principal sacred plant traditions carried within Paititi’s work: Ayahuasca, San Pedro or Wachuma, and Coca, each arising from a distinct ecological, cultural and cosmological context.

Ayahuasca is engaged within its Amazonian context and can support profound dimensions of healing, perception and relationship with the intelligence of nature, while San Pedro or Huachuma belongs to the ancient ceremonial traditions of the Andes and carries its own relationship with the mountains, the heart, the natural world and heightened human consciousness. Coca, one of the most sacred plants of the Andes, has been used for generations within prayer, offering, communication and reciprocal relationship with the land, community and the greater living world.

We do not approach these plants as interchangeable techniques for generating altered states, because each tradition carries a particular relationship, history and way of understanding the human journey. For the same reason, we do not predetermine a fixed number of ceremonies. The sequence and number of ceremonies are allowed to respond to the unfolding process and needs of the group, which has always been an essential principle within this retreat.

Individual Medicinal Plant Diets

Alongside the principal sacred plant traditions, participants may be introduced individually to other medicinal plants of the Amazon according to the needs of the retreat process. These relationships can support purification, sensitivity and introspection while helping cultivate particular natural qualities that may be relevant to an individual’s process.

Within the traditional understanding, a plant involves considerably more than consuming a medicinal botanical. The simplification of food, environment, stimulation and activity creates conditions in which greater sensitivity can develop, allowing the participant to enter into a subtler relationship with the plant, the surrounding ecosystem and their own organism.

Additional Practices and Support

The foundational practices and medicinal plant work are accompanied by Daoist Qigong and the Andean Art of Being, meditation, yoga and movement practices, sharing circles, creative expression, processing and reflection, nature immersion and Traditional Chinese Medicine when appropriate.

These modalities are not intended to function as unrelated techniques added to the retreat schedule. Qigong and movement support vitality and energetic alignment, sharing circles allow the universal process of consciousness transformation to be recognized through the unique experience of each participant, and Traditional Chinese Medicine can provide complementary support for energetic realignment when appropriate.

Their integration allows dreams, physical symptoms, ceremonial experiences, emotional processes and encounters with the natural environment to become different expressions of the same unfolding journey.

Initiation and the Hero’s Journey

The retreat is structured as a contemporary expression of a mystery initiation school – an ancient rite of passage in which an individual temporarily steps outside familiar structures, enters into a more direct relationship with the unknown and with forces greater than the conditioned personality, encounters the limitations that have shaped their experience, and gradually discovers a different relationship with themselves and life.

Across Indigenous and ancient cultures, such rites were understood as essential dimensions of human maturation. The Amazon provides a living environment in which this journey can become immediate rather than theoretical, particularly as many of the distractions through which we habitually regulate or avoid our inner experience are no longer available.

Within this process, participants are invited to recognize and work directly with habitual patterns, repressed emotions, fears, inhibitions, traumas and other energetic limitations while developing an increasingly embodied relationship with the qualities of awareness, loving kindness, clarity and responsibility that are inherent within our true nature. The heroic journey is therefore understood as a process of becoming increasingly human in a human body while consciously participating in the evolutionary potential carried within our lives.

The Amazon as Teacher

The rainforest is much more than the physical setting in which the retreat takes place. Immersion in one of the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth brings us into sustained relationship with a living intelligence that cannot be fully approached through conceptual understanding.

Away from the habitual stimulation and distractions of contemporary life, our senses gradually reorganize and we become increasingly aware of rhythms and relationships that ordinarily pass unnoticed. The Amazon reveals interdependence everywhere, through the continual relationship between plants, insects, animals, fungi, water, weather, decomposition and regeneration, all participating within a living system whose intelligence emerges through relationship rather than through any isolated part.

As sensitivity to this environment deepens, the apparent boundary between inner and outer nature can also become less rigid. Learning to understand Mother Nature’s language then becomes inseparable from learning to recognize the intelligence operating through our own organism, including the ways in which dreams, symptoms, emotions and intuitive perception communicate dimensions of experience that the conceptual mind may not immediately understand.

A Progressive 16-Day Journey

The sixteen-day container allows the retreat to unfold progressively according to the individual and collective process rather than compressing profound work into a predetermined sequence.

The initial phase establishes orientation, grounding, relationship with the environment and preparation, after which the foundational practices, medicinal plant relationships and ceremonial experiences progressively illuminate different dimensions of each participant’s journey. Periods of greater intensity are integrated through rest, movement, reflection, dreamwork, sharing, nature immersion and embodied practices, while the overall schedule remains responsive to the process because different individuals and groups require different rhythms.

As the retreat develops, increasing attention is given to recognizing and embodying one’s awakened potential and understanding how what has been discovered can continue in everyday life. Preparation, experience, recognition, integration and embodiment therefore continually inform one another rather than functioning as isolated stages.

Preparation and Integration Begin Before Arrival

Preparation is an essential part of the retreat process, and accepted participants receive detailed guidance concerning diet, medications and contraindications, travel preparation, what to bring and how to begin preparing psychologically and energetically before entering the Amazon.

Participants also receive lifelong access to Paititi’s self-paced online course, Your Evolutionary Blueprint, which provides a conceptual and experiential foundation for recognizing the process before arrival and continuing the integration afterward.

The foundational practices introduced during the retreat are intended to remain applicable throughout life. Remembrance, breathwork, dreamwork, movement, awareness and self-inquiry provide ways of continuing to engage what arises after leaving the Amazon, so that integration becomes less about explaining what happened during a ceremony and more about recognizing how the same evolutionary process continues communicating through relationships, family, work, creativity, challenges and the ordinary circumstances of one’s life.

Who This Retreat Is For

This immersion is intended for participants sincerely interested in a process of consciousness transformation and willing to take personal responsibility for that process. It may be particularly relevant for those moving through an important threshold in life, seeking to understand recurring emotional or relational patterns, feeling disconnected from deeper purpose or nature, integrating previous spiritual or psychedelic experiences, or wishing to engage ancestral living wisdom within a broader cultural and practical context.

Previous experience with meditation, breathwork or sacred plant traditions while very beneficial is not required, while a willingness to encounter new and unexpected challenges with sincerity, flexibility and a solutions-based attitude grounded in personal responsibility is an essential part of participating in the retreat.

Preparation, Health and Safety

This retreat involves an intensive physical, emotional and consciousness-oriented process, which is why participation is by application and health screening. We can accept participants who are in stable health, while minor health conditions may be compatible with participation depending on individual circumstances and should be discussed with us before applying.

All pharmaceutical medications, supplements and relevant health conditions must be disclosed, including any medications or supplements begun after registration. Many pharmaceutical medications are contraindicated with Amazonian and Andean plant medicines and may require specific periods of discontinuation before medicinal plant work can be considered, with every situation evaluated individually.

We do not recommend that anyone discontinue prescribed medication without the guidance of the physician or qualified healthcare professional overseeing their care.

For individuals with more significant health conditions, Paititi may recommend beginning through our three-month Distance Healing Program before evaluating whether participation in an in-person retreat is appropriate. Vaccinations chosen by participants should be completed no less than four weeks before the beginning of the retreat according to the existing program requirements.

Facilitated by Roman Hanis, Supported by the Paititi Team and Accompanied by a Yahua Elder

Paititi Institute co-founder Roman Hanis has lived and worked in close relationship with Indigenous communities and ancestral healing traditions of the Peruvian Amazon and Andes since 2001 and was adopted into the Yahua community early on in his journey.

His path has included long-term apprenticeship and relationship with Amazonian healing traditions alongside extensive study and practice in Traditional Chinese Medicine, Oriental bodywork, Jungian depth psychology, Tibetan contemplative traditions, breathwork and embodied approaches to transformation. Over more than two decades, these relationships have developed into an integral approach in which traditions are not treated as interchangeable or reduced to techniques, but are engaged through their respective contexts while illuminating different dimensions of the human evolutionary journey we all share.

Roman was featured in the critically acclaimed documentary The Sacred Science, filmed in 2010, and is the author of Beyond Ayahuasca, published by Hay House and an Amazon bestseller in the Shamanism category, which explores many of the principles underlying this work and the broader cultural context in which Amazonian plant medicine traditions exist.

The retreat is supported by the broader Paititi team and local partners and is accompanied by a Yahua elder, maintaining a living connection with the Indigenous community and lineage relationships through which this work has developed.

Accommodations and Location

We will be based at a traditional jungle center approximately one hour outside Iquitos, Peru, accessible only by boat and designed around simplicity and direct relationship with the rainforest. Many of the distractions through which we habitually avoid or regulate aspects of our inner experience are naturally reduced in this environment, making the physical setting itself an important dimension of the retreat.

The center consists of traditional Amazonian huts built on stilts above the ground, with wooden frames and mosquito-net walls that allow participants to remain intimately connected with the surrounding forest even while inside. Rooms are shared with one or two other participants of the same sex, and each participant is provided with a bed, bedding and mosquito net, while the rooms themselves have attached bathrooms.

We cannot guarantee private rooms, although when they are available they are offered on a first-come, first-served basis shortly before the retreat.

Food

Meals are natural and nourishing and are prepared according to the needs of the retreat and medicinal plant work, with diet understood as part of the process rather than simply a logistical consideration. Certain foods may be simplified or restricted at different stages in order to support medicinal plant relationships, physical purification and greater sensitivity.

Participants with significant food allergies or medical dietary requirements should disclose these during the application process so that we can determine beforehand what can safely be accommodated.

New Year in the Amazon

Crossing from one year into another creates a natural threshold within the sixteen-day journey and provides an opportunity to examine the deeper patterns from which our choices and intentions arise, including what we continue carrying from the previous year, what our experiences have been attempting to reveal, which patterns may have completed their purpose, and which qualities are seeking greater expression through our lives.

The transition from 2026 into 2027 therefore becomes part of the initiation itself, inviting us to enter the coming year with a clearer recognition of the evolutionary movement already taking place within our lives rather than approaching transformation only through another set of resolutions about what we believe should change.

Your Retreat Supports a Greater Purpose

Paititi Institute is a nonprofit organization working alongside Indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon and Andes at the intersection of cultural preservation, ecological stewardship, education, community health and human transformation, with retreats supporting this wider work throughout the Institute’s history.

Current initiatives include the development of Yahua and Q’ero Ancestral Schools, Indigenous cultural preservation and education, community health initiatives, ecological stewardship connected with Paititi’s 1,516-hectare biocultural reserve, and educational programs intended to support younger generations in maintaining relationship with living ancestral knowledge.

Participation in a retreat therefore enters a larger circle of reciprocity because the traditions and ecosystems making this work possible are living realities involving communities, territories, languages, elders, children and future generations. Paititi’s intention has always been to keep personal transformation connected with service, so that what we receive through these traditions can also contribute to their continuity.

Contribution

The contribution for the 16-day retreat is offered on a sliding scale of $2,333 to $2,777 USD and includes all food during the retreat, instruction, guidance and personal support, ceremonies, plant medicines and accommodation at the retreat center.

A 30% deposit is required at registration and is refunded if an applicant is not accepted into the retreat. Because the program requires a minimum number of participants, we determine whether this minimum has been reached four weeks before the starting date, and participants may wish to wait for this confirmation before purchasing non-refundable travel.

Please review the complete refund policy and Terms, Conditions, Release of Liability & Assumption of Risk before applying.

REFUND POLICY

Roman Hanis

Roman Hanis is an international bestselling author, healer, educator, and co-founder of Paititi Institute, a nonprofit organization dedicated to Indigenous cultural preservation, healing, education, and ecological stewardship.

Since arriving in the Peruvian Amazon in 2001, Roman has spent decades studying, practicing, and collaborating with Indigenous knowledge holders of the Amazon and Andes. His path has included long-term apprenticeship and relationship with Yahua, Huitoto, Ashuar, Shipibo and other Amazonian traditions, alongside ongoing study and practice within Andean lineages. In 2004, following several years of apprenticeship in the Amazon, he was formally recognized as a curandero by Yahua elders, a responsibility he continues to honor through healing work, cultural exchange, education, and community initiatives.

Roman is the author of Beyond Ayahuasca: Unlocking the Evolutionary Science of Indigenous Amazonian Wisdom to Access Your Highest Potential, published by Hay House. Drawing upon more than two decades of lived experience in the Amazon, the book brings ancestral approaches to healing into dialogue with Jungian psychology, trauma resolution, Eastern medicine, and contemplative practice. 100% of Roman’s author proceeds from the book support the development of the Yahua Ancestral School and Cultural Heritage Center in the Peruvian Amazon.

As co-founder of Paititi Institute, Roman has helped develop intercultural healing retreats, Indigenous community health and cultural exchange initiatives, educational programs, and ecological conservation projects in Peru and internationally. The Institute also stewards a 1,516-hectare biocultural reserve spanning Andean foothills and cloud rainforest near Manu National Park, protecting a landscape where biological and cultural diversity remain deeply interconnected.

Alongside his Amazonian and Andean apprenticeships, Roman has spent decades studying and practicing Jungian psychology, Tibetan Buddhist and Bön traditions, Daoist internal arts, and Traditional Chinese Medicine. His work explores the resonances between these distinct traditions without reducing their differences, bringing their practical methods into an experiential approach to healing, self-knowledge, and the realization of our intrinsic relationship with the living world.

Roman’s own recovery from a severe, life-threatening period of Crohn’s disease in 2002 became an important turning point in this path. Today, his work is centered on creating experiential bridges through which ancestral knowledge can remain a living transmission while supporting both individual transformation and the communities and ecosystems from which these traditions arise.

We are deeply inspired to announce the official launch of our online Home Study Course, “Your Evolutionary Blueprint” – an ongoing course that you can start anytime and approach it at your own pace!

In this interactive course you will explore your own heroic inner journey through life via video talks, reading materials, self inquiry & reflection homework, guided meditation, Primordial Breathwork, Alchemy QiGong and fun creative expression.

This adventurous curriculum guides you through transmission of indigenous living wisdom into the essential rites of passage of your daily life. Practical application of your highest creative potential is encouraged through Andean, Amazonian and Eastern perspectives. The intercultural bridges designed into this course connect the ancestral wisdom perspectives with Jungian Transpersonal approach in order to support everyone’s unique life journey towards wellbeing and a purposeful existence in a regenerative way.

Awakening the source of your creative expression takes place through transforming unresolved and stagnant emotional energies trapped in unprocessed key experiences of life. Remember yourself as the dreamer of reality, no longer a character lost in someone else’s dream.

 

Overview:

Every moment of our lives is communicating to us through the evolutionary language of nature. Our ancestors maintained a profound relationship with this ancient connection to all of life. The modern world has almost completely lost touch with this universal language even though it continues to knock on the doors of our perception through many challenges and adverse circumstances. Yet the crises can also be a catalyst of our greatest potential inviting greater wellbeing than we’ve ever imagined if only we can decipher the evolutionary language it speaks to us in. 

Throughout this course, you will explore the dreaming language, map your own heroic journey, and engage in the journey of remembrance of your true nature in order to come into your full potential, as the essential part of the Whole Organism that you are.

Shamanic / Transpersonal Dreamwork is a method to gain insights and receive communication from the subconscious that can bring us closer to wholeness, our true essence, and awaken our highest potential. Dreams are engaged in this context as evolutionary communication from the intelligence of our own organism. It’s an existential key to healing and transformation. This communication serves as an ongoing blueprint for your metamorphosis into a purposeful, fulfilling and joyful life. The elders of the Amazonian Ashuar Nation work with the dreams of individual tribe members as an evolutionary blueprint for the greater collective.  

Throughout dreams, the super-consciousness, our true nature, is speaking directly to the self in familiar associations and recognizable metaphors that also come through legends, fairy tales, and captivating classic stories of humanity. The reason these motifs are so captivating is because we feel ourselves vicariously living out our own heroic journey through someone else’s experience. 

Sacred Geometry can support us in building a relationship with this archetypal language of nature’s symbols. The proportions of our body, strands of our DNA, the cornea of our eye, snowflakes, pine cones, flower petals, crystals, the branching of trees, a sea shell, the orbit of the planets, the galaxy we spiral within, the air we breathe, and all life forms as we know them emerge out of timeless geometric codes.

The Pythagoreans consider the basic geometric forms to be the crystallized thoughts of the Creator. Through them we can start to unravel the basic archetypes found in nature through numbers and shapes to understand the deeper layers of subconscious communication offered in both our waking life and dreams.

The ancients knew that these patterns were symbolic codes of our own inner realm that ignite the soul’s fusion with form.  Drawing, viewing and contemplating these forms can allow us to gaze directly at the face of the infinite mystery and glimpse the inner workings of The Universal Heart/Mind. Through Sacred Geometry we can trace how universal energy can transform from emptiness to form and back again.

 

Course Curriculum

There are 5 chapters in the course, each designed to take a week. However, the course is flexible and you can work at your own pace. Some may go through it faster (not too fast) and some slower (not too slow).

Chapter 1: The Call to Evolve
Chapter 2: Crossing the Line of No Return
Chapter 3 – Remembering The Infinite
Chapter 4: Finding the Way Through Patterns of Evolution
Chapter 5: Emerging From the Dark Night of the Soul
Post Course: Community Forum Engagement

9 hours of video teachings

Two downloadable booklets & one book

5 in-depth chapters

Reflection homework activities

Supported Discussion Forum (available to all participants who complete the course work)


+Bonus Material

We wish to make this available to anyone who has a sincere inspiration in these challenging times. If you’re not able to make the minimum contribution, we welcome you to fill out our scholarship application HERE >>

About the Learning Platform: 

This course is held through an interactive online learning platform called Sutra. It has been adapted from a live course we held via Zoom with additional, in-depth resources and instructions added to support each person through a more interactive and immersive journey. At the end of the course material all participants will be invited to engage their insights within a community forum of those who have also completed the course.

Frequently Asked Questions:

What is the purpose of this course?
This course is designed for those who wish to embody a more genuine sense of being, empowered to work with all circumstances of life. Are you ready to no longer be a passive passenger and take responsibility for designing your life with a creative, joyful and caring perspective in all situations?

What does transformation entail?
Transformation starts with a shift in perspective. We may hold concepts or ideas that are not supportive of our wellbeing. On this heroic path the conceptual frame of engaging with the world is transformed through a complete paradigm shift.

Who is this course for?
This course is particularly helpful for anyone at a crossroad in life who wishes to get to the root of life’s essence. This work can enhance and deepen your embodiment and connection to the essence of any spiritual approach already engaged with.

For those who have had profound mind altering experiences and/or are immersed in ceremony work, this course is a profound integration tool to support understanding your experiences more deeply and applying them to each moment. See what your life is really about.

What are the benefits of this online format?
We love working with people in person, however through the years we’ve found a gap between the retreats and everyday life which can be hard to bridge. One of the purposes of this course is to offer a tool to fill this gap. Unlike a retreat where we step out of our habitual environment, this course is brought into your everyday environment.

When does the course begin?
The course is self-paced, so you can get started as soon as you enroll and go at your own pace.

How long will the discussion boards be available?
The discussion board will become available for your engagement once you complete the course work. Access is unlimited.

Can I still take this course without a desktop/laptop computer (for example, if I only have an iPad)?
Yes, you can access this course using the Sutra mobil app called “Sutra Spaces” on your phone or using your internet browser on a tablet.

What if I have technical difficulties with the course?
Our course hosts at Sutra are available for technical support if issues arise.

teacher_objects.post_content:
Since childhood, Cynthia Robinson has had a deep love for nature and natural healing. She always knew she would devote her life in service to the healing of people and the planet.

Cynthia got her BA at the University of Michigan School of Art and Design with a focus in Design, Communication and Creative Problem Solving. After graduation, she pursued her passion to bring deeper values for nature and humanity into the world working as a brand strategist and designer supporting both Fortune 500 as well as smaller companies to implement Permaculture thinking into their infrastructure, product designs and marketing.

Working in the corporate world of New York City led her to discover a more profound passion to support herself and others in establishing deeper connection to nature, ancestral values and unlocking our highest potential as human beings. She traded in the corporate boardrooms for 100 acres in the middle of the Amazon Rainforest where she co-founded the Paititi Institute for the Preservation of the Amazon Rainforest and Indigenous Culture.

At Paititi, Cynthia works alongside her partners to create a platform that practically applies ancient wisdom to our modern world, building intercultural bridges for healing on physical, emotional and spiritual levels for all people from all cultures and all spiritual traditions. She currently works to develop and facilitate holistic experiential education models, weaving together our inner and outer landscapes through nature awareness, traditional Permaculture education, health education and indigenous Amazonian teachings and practices integrated with ancestral wisdom from around the planet.

In addition, in her role as Paititi’s Director of Permaculture, Cynthia is in charge of establishing tropical permaculture models on-site, while cultivating an intentional community that implements ongoing outreach projects in local native villages and tribes. Some of these projects’ focus include: appropriate technology for sanitation and clean water, fair trade exports, and cultural healing exchange programs which establish natural medicine clinics.

Finally, Cynthia is currently in the process of being initiated into Indigenous Amazonian Healing practices to become a medicine woman and carry on this ancient lineage of healing wisdom.

Roman Hanis

Roman Hanis is an international bestselling author, healer, educator, and co-founder of Paititi Institute, a nonprofit organization dedicated to Indigenous cultural preservation, healing, education, and ecological stewardship.

Since arriving in the Peruvian Amazon in 2001, Roman has spent decades studying, practicing, and collaborating with Indigenous knowledge holders of the Amazon and Andes. His path has included long-term apprenticeship and relationship with Yahua, Huitoto, Ashuar, Shipibo and other Amazonian traditions, alongside ongoing study and practice within Andean lineages. In 2004, following several years of apprenticeship in the Amazon, he was formally recognized as a curandero by Yahua elders, a responsibility he continues to honor through healing work, cultural exchange, education, and community initiatives.

Roman is the author of Beyond Ayahuasca: Unlocking the Evolutionary Science of Indigenous Amazonian Wisdom to Access Your Highest Potential, published by Hay House. Drawing upon more than two decades of lived experience in the Amazon, the book brings ancestral approaches to healing into dialogue with Jungian psychology, trauma resolution, Eastern medicine, and contemplative practice. 100% of Roman’s author proceeds from the book support the development of the Yahua Ancestral School and Cultural Heritage Center in the Peruvian Amazon.

As co-founder of Paititi Institute, Roman has helped develop intercultural healing retreats, Indigenous community health and cultural exchange initiatives, educational programs, and ecological conservation projects in Peru and internationally. The Institute also stewards a 1,516-hectare biocultural reserve spanning Andean foothills and cloud rainforest near Manu National Park, protecting a landscape where biological and cultural diversity remain deeply interconnected.

Alongside his Amazonian and Andean apprenticeships, Roman has spent decades studying and practicing Jungian psychology, Tibetan Buddhist and Bön traditions, Daoist internal arts, and Traditional Chinese Medicine. His work explores the resonances between these distinct traditions without reducing their differences, bringing their practical methods into an experiential approach to healing, self-knowledge, and the realization of our intrinsic relationship with the living world.

Roman’s own recovery from a severe, life-threatening period of Crohn’s disease in 2002 became an important turning point in this path. Today, his work is centered on creating experiential bridges through which ancestral knowledge can remain a living transmission while supporting both individual transformation and the communities and ecosystems from which these traditions arise.

courses.text_full:
We are inspired to share this Primordial Breathwork™: Online Home Study Course Series in accessible virtual format as an encouragement for awakening greater vitality in your life. This series focuses on the first portion of the Primordial Breathwork™ inspired by the Amazonian rainforest tribal culture which has been beneficial to us and many in our community during trying times. The breathwork sessions are guided by Roman Hanis who has facilitated this practice since 2003.

These practices are considered to be essential steps in remembering our greatest natural potential by opening the energy channels of the organism allowing for deeper connection with the vital power of the inherent intelligence inside and out.

 

Course Curriculum:

There are 2 informational talks and 5 video practice sessions in the course. We recommend coming back to the practice often, as it is cumulative and will deepen as you continue to engage.

Chapter 1 – Intro to your True Self via Primordial Breathwork
Chapter 2 – The Interconnectedness Of Your Own Being
Chapter 3 – Breathing Wellness Into Every Moment of Life
Chapter 4 – The Elemental Energy Centers of Your Emotional Wellness
Chapter 5 – Remembering the True Nature of Breath

Course Summary:

• 5 active practice sessions (over 4 hours in total)

• 3 hours of theory and philosophy as foundational support to deepen your practice further and integrate it with everyday life

• Guided remembrance meditation & accompanying booklet 

• Original sound clip of Yanomami tribe engaging in a more intuitive version of this breath work

• Reflection and integration activities

• Supported Discussion Forum

Benefits of the Course: 

• Rekindle your original connection with the essence of vitality by awakening inherently natural, higher vibrational frequencies of your organism.

• Eliminates stress and opens deeper states of presence in our day to day life

• The practice aids in the location and elimination of psychosomatic sources of tensions, inhibitions and repressed emotions

• The practice helps to connect to bio-electro magnetic field of the earth, let go of stress and anxiety and reset the natural bio-rhythms of the organism to the original state. 

Contribution:

This course contribution is $30-150 sliding scale. We welcome you to contribute the amount that is accessible for you.

We wish to make this available to anyone who has a sincere inspiration in these challenging times. If you’re not able to make the minimum contribution, we welcome you to fill out our scholarship application HERE >>

About the Learning Platform:

This course is held through an interactive online learning platform called Sutra. It has been adapted from a live course we held via Zoom with additional, in-depth resources and instructions added to support each person through a more interactive and immersive journey.

Frequently Asked Questions:

Benefits of this online format:
We love working with people in person, however through the years we’ve found a gap between retreats and everyday life- which can be hard to bridge. One of the purposes of this course is to offer a practical tool to fill this gap. Unlike a retreat where we step out of our habitual environment, this course can be brought into your everyday environment.

When does the course begin?
The course is open registration and self-paced, so you can get started as soon as you enroll and engage at your own pace.

How long will the discussion boards be available?
An ongoing discussion board is available where you can ask questions and share your reflections. Access is unlimited.

Can I still take this course without a desktop/laptop computer (for example, if I only have an iPad)?
Yes, you can access this course using the Sutra mobil app on your phone or using your internet browser on a tablet.

What if I have technical difficulties with the course?
Our course hosts at Sutra are available for technical support if issues arise.

courses.text_full:
Beyond Ayahuasca book: The Practical Trilogy + Bonus Practice

 

Our wholehearted gift to our friends around the world who by buying the book are supporting the Indigenous Yahua nation ancestral school development in the Peruvian Amazon Rainforest.

After registering please send a screenshot of your book purchase proof to our email Info@Paititi-Institute.org

 

This experiential course is a living extension of the Beyond Ayahuasca book—a pathway where ancient wisdom becomes embodied truth. You’ll be guided through three core Indigenous practices rooted in the sacred traditions shared in the book: Primordial Breathwork, Alchemy of Immortality Qigong/Andean Art of Being, and Ancestral Remembrance Meditation. These practices are portals into ancestral knowledge and deep inner transformation.

Alongside these, Robin Lyons offers a powerful bonus practice—an integration of movement, presence, and inspiration—designed to help you weave this wisdom into the fabric of your everyday life. Her unique gift for sparking aliveness meets Roman Hanis’s deep transmissions of ancestral wisdom, creating a synergy that invites both awakening and grounded embodiment.

Together, these offerings support personal healing and collective evolution—while also directly empowering the Yahua Nation’s efforts to protect and pass on their sacred traditions through the Amazonian Ancestral School.

Walk the path. Embody the wisdom. Support the Earth’s guardians.
______________________________________________________________________________________________

🌬 Primordial Breathwork™

Rooted in the sacred lineages of the Amazonian Yanomami nation, this breathwork practice is a gateway to the subconscious and the spirit world. You will be guided to awaken the seven elemental centers within, unlocking emotional healing, expanded awareness, and deep clarity. This is not just a breath practice—it is an ancestral ceremony of remembrance through your own body and breath.

Purpose: Reconnect with your true nature and clear emotional blockages by aligning your breath with the primordial elements of life.

🌿 Alchemy of Immortality Qigong / Andean Art of Being

This ancient energy cultivation practice harmonizes body, mind, and spirit by awakening the three primary energy centers—lower (vitality), middle (emotions), and upper (spiritual insight). Adapted to integrate Indigenous Amazonian and Eastern wisdom, this Qigong guides you to restore balance and vitality, while cultivating the inner qualities of presence, clarity, and compassion.

Purpose: Activate life-force energy and embody spiritual presence through conscious movement and internal alchemy.

🌀 Ancestral Remembrance Meditation

A sacred practice revealed in Beyond Ayahuasca, this guided meditation is an invitation to reconnect with the spirit of your lineage and the original wisdom encoded in your being. Through stillness and visionary awareness, you will open to direct communion with ancestral guidance, restoring the soul threads that have been lost or forgotten.

Purpose: Remember your roots, awaken ancient memory, and restore spiritual continuity with the Earth and your ancestors.

🔥 Bonus Practice: Embodied Integration with Robin Lyons

This exclusive bonus offering brings all three core practices into a unified whole. Robin’s unique gift lies in her ability to translate deep wisdom into embodied, joyful presence. Her movement-based integration practice anchors your transformation into daily life—so the sacred isn’t left on the cushion, but walks with you in every moment.

Purpose: Ground your healing journey in everyday reality and awaken the aliveness that brings the sacred into all you do.

About the Learning Platform: 

This course is held through an interactive online learning platform called Sutra. It has been adapted from a live course we held via Zoom with additional, in-depth resources and instructions added to support each person through a more interactive and immersive journey. At the end of the course material all participants will be invited to engage their insights within a community forum of those who have also completed the course.

Frequently Asked Questions:

What is the purpose of this course?
This course is designed for those who wish to embody a more genuine sense of being, empowered to work with all circumstances of life. Are you ready to no longer be a passive passenger and take responsibility for designing your life with a creative, joyful and caring perspective in all situations?

What does transformation entail?
Transformation starts with a shift in perspective. We may hold concepts or ideas that are not supportive of our wellbeing. On this heroic path the conceptual frame of engaging with the world is transformed through a complete paradigm shift.

Who is this course for?
This course is particularly helpful for anyone at a crossroad in life who wishes to get to the root of life’s essence. This work can enhance and deepen your embodiment and connection to the essence of any spiritual approach already engaged with.

For those who have had profound mind altering experiences and/or are immersed in ceremony work, this course is a profound integration tool to support understanding your experiences more deeply and applying them to each moment. See what your life is really about.

What are the benefits of this online format?
We love working with people in person, however through the years we’ve found a gap between the retreats and everyday life which can be hard to bridge. One of the purposes of this course is to offer a tool to fill this gap. Unlike a retreat where we step out of our habitual environment, this course is brought into your everyday environment.

When does the course begin?
The course is self-paced, so you can get started as soon as you enroll and go at your own pace.

How long will the discussion boards be available?
The discussion board will become available for your engagement once you complete the course work. Access is unlimited.

Can I still take this course without a desktop/laptop computer (for example, if I only have an iPad)?
Yes, you can access this course using the Sutra mobil app called “Sutra Spaces” on your phone or using your internet browser on a tablet.

What if I have technical difficulties with the course?

teacher_objects.name: Robin Lyons
teacher_objects.text: Robin Lyons has been a strength and conditioning coach for over 23 years coaching all types of individuals from elite athletes to weekend warriors and stay at home moms. Her extensive background in competitive sport, human physiology and holistic practices has crafted her coaching philosophy to address the why behind the prescription. “I believe every individual innately wants to live their highest potential. To do this they must first identify what is limiting their wellbeing, health, and function. The “why” behind what they do needs to go beyond external motivation. Facing oneself and taking full responsibility will provide the internal drive to walk a path that is aligned with their highest values and purpose.” Robin’s coaching philosophy is that every athlete is unique, and therefore every athlete needs to be coached in a way which is suitable for them. Meeting each athlete where they are currently allows for long-term success. Robin works with individuals who want to evolve as individuals through learning more about themselves, their body and emotions. Robin Lyons is the owner/ founder of MTN LAB Holistic Performance Coaching. She currently coaches people remotely and in person in her small training studio in Driggs Idaho.
